accounting.rationale: EQUIVALENCE cannot cause the storage sequences of two different common blocks to be associated.
The cause is an EQUIVALENCE statement.
The blocks are different, including named versus blank.
Association of their sequences is prohibited.
Equivalence association cannot place a default-initialized derived object in association with a COMMON object.
The prohibition concerns association through EQUIVALENCE.
The relevant associated object is of derived type.
Its type has default initialization under7.5.4.6p8.
It must not thereby associate with an object in common.
Equivalence extension of a common block cannot add storage units before the first unit of its first listed object.
The condition is caused by equivalence association.
The sequence being extended belongs to a common block.
The prohibited addition concerns storage units, not bytes.
No added unit may precede the relevant first unit.
The reference point is the first object specified for that block.
The first object is determined from the actual COMMON declarations.

requirements.title: EQUIVALENCE does not join two different common blocks
requirements.definition: An EQUIVALENCE statement cannot cause the storage sequences of two different common blocks to become associated. Direct and indirect association consequences matter; repeated declarations of one block name within a scope are not two different blocks.

pending.two-named-blocks: PENDING a complete INTEGER-only program declares COMMON /left_block/ a and COMMON /right_block/ b, then EQUIVALENCE(a,b). Delete only EQUIVALENCE for the control. Keep both distinct block declarations and no initialization, TARGET, pointer, SAVE conflict or payload read.
pending.named-and-blank: PENDING the same complete structure has a in named COMMON and b in blank COMMON. Remove only their EQUIVALENCE for the valid control. The result cannot be justified by different named/blank size rules or by a linker merging symbols.
pending.transitive-bridge: PENDING a complete source uses the same two blocks plus a local INTEGER bridge and EQUIVALENCE(a,bridge),(bridge,b). Remove only the second set to stop joining the blocks, preserving a valid first set. Source-review the whole chain, C8110-C8120 and8.10.1.5; do not count only pairs containing two textual COMMON member names.

requirements.title: A default-initialized derived object is not equivalenced into COMMON
requirements.definition: Equivalence association cannot associate a derived object with default initialization with an object in COMMON. Direct listing under C8124 is a different source route. Default initialization is determined from the full applicable type definition, not merely an outer declaration or whether the program later overwrites the value.

pending.direct-default-initializer: PENDING a complete program defines a SEQUENCE type with INTEGER :: field=7, declares an object local_record, puts an ordinary INTEGER member in named COMMON, and uses EQUIVALENCE(member,local_record). Remove only =7 from the type component for the control. The derived object is not itself an R877 list entry; no explicit initialization or undefined value read is added.
pending.nested-default-initializer: PENDING complete nested numeric SEQUENCE definitions have a default-initialized INTEGER behind a nonpointer nonallocatable derived component. Equivalence to an ordinary COMMON member is the same forbidden condition; remove only the nested initializer. Retain the recursive direct-component/default-init source proof.
pending.indirect-association-and-overlap: PENDING extend a complete ordinary-INTEGER/SEQUENCE source through a local bridge EQUIVALENCE chain before reaching COMMON. The repair removes the component initializer without changing the association graph. Pointer/allocatable-component types require separate C8110 eligibility and cannot stand in as an isolated control; direct COMMON listing retains C8124.

requirements.title: Equivalence extension of COMMON cannot precede its first storage unit
requirements.definition: Equivalence association cannot enlarge a common-block sequence by adding units before the first unit of the first object specified for that block in COMMON.8.10.2.2p1's tail-only condition is accounted under this same owner. Eligible tail extension remains possible and contributes to the size of the block.

pending.direct-backward-extension: PENDING a complete program declares INTEGER first, extension(2), COMMON /packet/ first and EQUIVALENCE(first,extension(2)). Change only subscript2 to1 for the valid tail-extension control. Bounds are constant and in range in both sources; no address, layout or uninitialized payload is inspected.
pending.transitive-backward-extension: PENDING a complete source adds INTEGER bridge, then EQUIVALENCE(first,bridge),(bridge,extension(2)). The same one-subscript repair removes the pre-first unit through the full chain. Keep8.10.1.5 repeated/nonconsecutive-unit restrictions and avoid accidentally joining two different blocks.
pending.blank-common-boundary: PENDING the direct complete source/control uses blank COMMON instead of a named block. Its allowed interscope size variation does not permit local pre-first-unit extension. The first specified object and actual storage sequence remain explicit.

review_rationale: Independent original-source review925b4227 and all10pending plans in doc/source_audits/batch_084.json. The three prose restrictions forbid joining distinct common blocks, equivalencing default-initialized derived objects into COMMON and extending before the first specified storage unit, including indirect chains. The default-init contrast keeps the derived object outside the COMMON list and removes only its initializer. Direct/transitive tail controls preserve other EQUIVALENCE eligibility and sequence constraints.
